source.title: Align, Unify, Suppress, Route: A Coherentist View of Transformer Computation

page_placements.theme: Post-pretraining training preserves or strengthens induction and retrieval heads

record.tranche_reason: Measures induction-head score correlations in base/instruction-tuned model pairs, extending the analysis to several model families and post-training variants; it does not reproduce the original training-time emergence or in-context-learning measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper describes induction heads as a known mechanism, citing prior work, but does not test their composition mechanism, training-time formation, or in-context-learning effects. Its own induction-related result is the P4 comparison of induction-head score correlations across four base/instruction-tuned pairs. Other operator and coherence results are not induction or in-context-learning measurements.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its only induction result (P4, Section 5.6, Table 4) is a Pearson correlation of per-head induction scores between base and instruction-tuned variants. That is a preservation or stability measure, not evidence that heads with induction behaviour form or exist. A high correlation is possible without strong induction heads, and the paper reports no absolute induction scores, head counts or [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour. It uses induction heads as a known mechanism cited from Olsson et al. 2022. It runs no training-time, in-context-learning or few-shot analyses. Its 'alignment' detector uses previous-token and duplicate-token attention, not induction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find induction-head score structure preserved after instruction tuning in all four pairs (r≥0.98). The operator-specific late-shift prediction holds only in the two LLaMA pairs (SUPPORT) and not in Gemma or Qwen (PARTIAL). Their claim that post-training leaves base in-context circuits intact is an interpretation; they did not test in-context behaviour directly.
record.recipe_differences: Uses correlations of corresponding-head induction scores across base/instruction-tuned pairs, rather than testing induction-head formation or in-context-learning changes during training.
record.method_sensitivity: The induction-score comparison covers only the four available base/instruction-tuned pairs; the paper reports no consistent shift in the tested score structure across those pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-head induction-score structure is highly correlated between base and instruction-tuned variants in Gemma-2B, LLaMA-1B, LLaMA-3B and Qwen-1.5B (r=0.982–0.998). Each pair passes a one-sided test against r=0.9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction tuning preserves the per-head distribution of induction scores established in pretraining.

record.problems: The induction-related evidence is limited to score correlations in four base/instruction-tuned pairs, rather than direct behavioral validation or a training-time study. The reported correlations establish score preservation in those pairs, not universality across independent training runs, all sizes, or other architectures and modalities.

untested.parts: No test of previous-token composition or the copying mechanism; the mechanism is only described from prior work (Section 3.4).
No training-time analysis, no in-context-learning curve, no loss bump.
No measurement of in-context learning or of induction heads' share of it.
No absolute induction scores or counts of induction heads per model; only cross-variant score correlations in four pairs.
No manipulation of data or training setup; instruction tuning is compared only for score preservation, not for formation or in-context-learning persistence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is dropped: a correlation of scores across variants does not show that induction heads appear. The paper reports no absolute induction-score magnitudes. The 15-model operator, coherence and ablation results do not concern induction heads or in-context learning.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test composition with a previous-token head or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying behavior.
No training-time formation sweep, abruptness measure, in-context-learning loss-by-token-index measure, or training-loss bump analysis.
Does not measure induction heads as the mechanism behind most in-context learning in large transformers.

Tests score-structure preservation in four base/instruction-tuned pairs only; it does not establish direct behavioral induction-head presence across independent training runs, all model sizes or families, or other architectures and modalities.
Does not test how data or training setup affects induction-head formation or the persistence of in-context learning.
Does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.
Does not investigate whether induction-head formation consists of multiple transitions.

relation.reason: Uses the established induction mechanism to interpret operator roles; the base-versus-tuned correlations do not measure induction-head presence, formation, or causal contributions to in-context learning.

tranche.reason: Uses induction circuitry within the CPC framework and measures score preservation after post-training, a stability construct that does not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 4 reports means over five seeds; all four preservation tests pass at p<0.05. Its SUPPORT/PARTIAL verdicts concern CPC's combined P4 prediction, not the catalog's induction-head claim versions.
